cues.en: Mike: In this video, I'm going to introduce you to two important and related mathematical functions, and those are the natural exponent and the logarithm.
cues.zh: 這部影片，我要介紹兩個重要而且相關的數學函數：自然指數函數與對數函數。

cues.en: These are actually intimately related to each other.
cues.zh: 它們其實有非常密切的關係。

cues.en: And I will show you that these two functions are inverses of each other.
cues.zh: 我會說明，這兩個函數互為反函數。

cues.en: Now, if this were a math course, we could spend hours talking about the intricacies of the natural exponent and the natural logarithm, and logarithms to different bases.
cues.zh: 如果是數學課，可以花好幾個小時，討論自然指數、自然對數，以及不同底數對數的細節。

cues.en: But in this video, I'm gonna focus on a more visual and intuitive understanding.
cues.zh: 但這部影片，我要著重在視覺與直覺上的理解。

cues.en: Now, before I begin, I want to first discuss some notations, which can make things a little bit confusing and mea culpa, I must admit that I also am,
cues.zh: 開始之前，先談一些記法，這可能讓事情有點混淆。我得承認，我自己也，

cues.en: certainly in this video and probably in other videos, occasionally mixing these two notations.
cues.zh: 至少在這部影片，以及大概其他影片，偶爾會混用這兩種記法。

cues.en: And, well, I apologize for making that a little more confusing.
cues.zh: 抱歉，這讓事情更令人困惑一點。

cues.en: But, you know, that's just how it goes when you're integrating math and coding.
cues.zh: 不過，整合數學與程式設計時，就是會有這種情況。

cues.en: Okay, so this is the notation for the natural exponent.
cues.zh: 這是自然指數的記法。

cues.en: In math notation, it's e to the x.
cues.zh: 數學記號寫成 e 的 x 次方。

cues.en: And in code, it's exp(x).
cues.zh: 程式碼寫成 exp(x)。

cues.en: So these two are comparable.
cues.zh: 所以兩者相對應。

cues.en: This is MATLAB code, of course, if you're doing this in Python, then you just add an np, right?
cues.zh: 這當然是 MATLAB 程式碼。如果用 Python，只要加上 np，對吧？

cues.en: So this would be np dot x.
cues.zh: 所以會是 np.exp(x)。

cues.en: So, that's not too confusing.
cues.zh: 這還不太令人困惑。

cues.en: It starts getting confusing with the logarithms.
cues.zh: 到了對數，就開始混淆了。

cues.en: So, in math notation, the logs different bases, are indicated as the word log, you write out log, and then in subscripted letters, the base,
cues.zh: 數學記號中，不同底數的對數，會寫出 log，再用下標寫出底數，

cues.en: so this is log base 10, in code, it's log10.
cues.zh: 所以這是以 10 為底的對數，程式碼則是 log10。

cues.en: So that part is actually not confusing.
cues.zh: 這部分其實不令人混淆。

cues.en: What is confusing is that the natural log in math notation is indicated as ln, but in code it's still just log.
cues.zh: 令人混淆的是，自然對數在數學上寫成 ln，但程式碼裡仍然只寫 log。

cues.en: So, this is actually the natural logarithm.
cues.zh: 所以這其實是自然對數。

cues.en: This is equivalent. These two expressions are equivalent.
cues.zh: 兩者相等，這兩個算式等價。

cues.en: This is just a commonly used shorthand in math, which has the same meaning as log base e.
cues.zh: 這只是數學中常用的簡寫，意思和以 e 為底的對數相同。

cues.en: So you'll see in the slides in this video, that I sometimes write out log(x), when I'm actually referring to the natural log.
cues.zh: 所以你會看到這部影片投影片上，有時我寫 log(x)，其實指的是自然對數。

cues.en: So, whenever you have the word log without any numbers after it or subscripts after it, you can assume that it is log base e,
cues.zh: 看到 log 後面沒有數字或下標時，可以假設它是以 e 為底的對數，

cues.en: which is the natural logarithm.
cues.zh: 也就是自然對數。

cues.en: So a little bit about notation there.
cues.zh: 以上是一些記法說明。

cues.en: So, here you see a plot of y = e to the x.
cues.zh: 這裡是 y=e 的 x 次方的圖。

cues.en: So we have x on the x-axis.
cues.zh: x 軸是 x。

cues.en: And the y-axis, is the function e to the power of x.
cues.zh: y 軸是 e 的 x 次方這個函數。

cues.en: So, this is an exponentially increasing function, that's why it's called the natural exponent.
cues.zh: 這是呈指數增加的函數，因此叫做自然指數函數。

cues.en: And there's a couple of important properties of e, so the natural exponent, that are worth committing to memory.
cues.zh: e，也就是自然指數，有幾個重要性質值得記住。

cues.en: First of all, this letter e, it stands for an irrational number.
cues.zh: 首先，字母 e 代表一個無理數。

cues.en: So it's a number that never ends.
cues.zh: 也就是小數展開永遠不會結束的數。

cues.en: And it is 2.78 something, something, something.
cues.zh: 它是 2.78，再接其他數字。

cues.en: So, a few things to note about e to the x, the function e to the x, one is that, it is never negative.
cues.zh: 關於 e 的 x 次方這個函數，有幾點要注意。其中一點是，它永遠不會是負數。

cues.en: It never gets to be a negative number.
cues.zh: 永遠不會得到負數。

cues.en: And furthermore, it never even gets to be 0.
cues.zh: 而且，甚至永遠不會等於 0。

cues.en: It gets very, very, very close to 0, arbitrarily close to 0.
cues.zh: 它會非常非常接近 0，可以任意接近 0。

cues.en: On computers, it becomes indistinguishable from 0 with some precision errors around computer rounding errors.
cues.zh: 在電腦上，由於精度誤差、四捨五入誤差，它會變得與 0 無法區分。

cues.en: But in theory, e to the x never actually gets to be 0, as x goes to minus infinity.
cues.zh: 但理論上，即使 x 趨近負無限大，e 的 x 次方也永遠不會真正等於 0。

cues.en: On the plus side, when x goes positive, e to the x grows really, really large, really, really fast.
cues.zh: 正的方向，當 x 變大，e 的 x 次方會非常非常快地變得非常大。

cues.en: It blows up to positive infinity very, very quickly.
cues.zh: 很快就會暴增到正無限大。

cues.en: And it's also interesting to keep in mind that when x equals 0, e to the x equals 1.
cues.zh: 另一個值得記住的有趣性質，是 x=0 時，e 的 x 次方等於 1。

cues.en: And that's because, as I mentioned a few videos ago, any number to the power of 0 is 1.
cues.zh: 因為前幾部影片說過，任何數的 0 次方都等於 1。

cues.en: So this function, so y equals 1, when e to the x, or for e to the x where x equals 0.
cues.zh: 所以在 e 的 x 次方這個函數中，x=0 時，y=1。

cues.en: So e to the x basically grows really, really quickly.
cues.zh: e 的 x 次方，基本上會非常快速地增長。

cues.en: Now, e to the x, the natural exponent, appears all over mathematics and all over applied mathematics.
cues.zh: 自然指數函數 e 的 x 次方，在數學與應用數學中隨處可見。

cues.en: You see it in growth curves, you see it in finance, you see it in navigation, you see it in trigonometry.
cues.zh: 成長曲線、金融、導航、三角學，都會看到。

cues.en: Has many interesting properties, including, for example, that the derivative of e to the x is also e to the x.
cues.zh: 它有很多有趣性質，例如 e 的 x 次方的導數，仍然是 e 的 x 次方。

cues.en: Now, a lot of these more advanced concepts for e, natural exponent, are not relevant for us.
cues.zh: 不過，e 與自然指數的很多進階概念，與我們這裡無關。

cues.en: Now, the important things that you need to know for this course is that e to the power of something, so e to the x, is a non-negative function,
cues.zh: 這門課需要知道的重要概念，是 e 的某次方，也就是 e 的 x 次方，是非負函數，

cues.en: and it very, very quickly blows up to plus infinity.
cues.zh: 而且會非常快速地暴增到正無限大。

cues.en: And then we have, you know, it's kind of like the evil twin brother of the natural exponent, which is the natural logarithm.
cues.zh: 接著是自然指數有點像邪惡雙胞胎兄弟的函數，也就是自然對數。

cues.en: And it almost looks like, you know, it looks a little bit like you just flip this function over, like, you're just, you know, mirroring or reflecting this function.
cues.zh: 它看起來有點像把這個函數翻過來，好像鏡射或反射這個函數。

cues.en: So this function, log(x), natural log of x, actually does become negative.
cues.zh: 這個函數 log(x)，也就是 x 的自然對數，確實會變成負數。

cues.en: In fact, it quickly goes down to minus infinity as x approaches 0.
cues.zh: 事實上，當 x 趨近 0，它會迅速降到負無限大。

cues.en: Now, x here, cannot...
cues.zh: 這裡的 x 不能……

cues.en: Or I should say, the function here is not defined for negative values of x.
cues.zh: 應該說，這個函數在 x 為負值時沒有定義。

cues.en: So you cannot take the logarithm of a negative number that doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 所以不能對負數取對數，那沒有意義。

cues.en: You just get minus infinity or minus not a number.
cues.zh: 只會得到負無限大，或負的非數值。

cues.en: I forget which one.
cues.zh: 我忘記是哪個了。

cues.en: And the log of x on the positive side, as x continues to grow larger, this does creep up to infinity.
cues.zh: 在正的方向，當 x 持續變大，log(x) 也會慢慢增長到無限大。

cues.en: It just keeps growing.
cues.zh: 它會不斷增長。

cues.en: But you can see it's growing slower and slower.
cues.zh: 但可以看到，增長得越來越慢。

cues.en: So the larger x becomes, the more slowly log of x will grow.
cues.zh: x 越大，log(x) 增長得越慢。

cues.en: Now, in statistics, log of x, the natural algorithm, is often used to describe differences in probabilities between very small numbers.
cues.zh: 統計中，log(x)，也就是自然對數，經常用來描述非常小的數字之間的機率差異。

cues.en: And you can see why that's the case.
cues.zh: 你可以看出原因。

cues.en: So imagine you are trying to distinguish between two probability values that are very close to each other, maybe 0.01 and 0.02.
cues.zh: 想像要分辨兩個非常接近的機率值，例如 0.01 和 0.02。

cues.en: Now, those numbers are very close to each other, but the logarithm of those numbers is further apart.
cues.zh: 這兩個數非常接近，但它們的對數相隔更遠。

cues.en: So I will discuss this later on.
cues.zh: 之後會再討論。

cues.en: I think maybe even in the next video.
cues.zh: 我想，可能下一部影片就會談到。

cues.en: But the logarithm is very useful for distinguishing between very small numbers that are very close to 0, positive numbers.
cues.zh: 不過，對於區分非常接近 0 的小正數，對數非常有用。

cues.en: Now, one interesting thing about e and log, so the natural exponent and the natural logarithm, is that they're perfect inverses of each other.
cues.zh: e 與 log，也就是自然指數與自然對數，有個有趣性質：兩者恰好互為反函數。

cues.en: So that means that you can use them to basically negate each other or to cancel each other out.
cues.zh: 也就是說，基本上能用它們互相抵銷。

cues.en: Here you see an illustration of that.
cues.zh: 這裡是示意圖。

cues.en: So, if we would plot y1 by y2, where y1 is defined as the logarithm of e to the x, and y2 is defined as e to the logarithm of x,
cues.zh: 如果畫出 y1 對 y2，其中 y1 定義為 e 的 x 次方的對數，y2 定義為 e 的 log(x) 次方，

cues.en: where x goes from basically just a little bit above 0 up to 10, then it turns out that we get a straight line here.
cues.zh: x 從略大於 0 一直到 10，結果就會得到這條直線。

cues.en: And the reason why we get a straight line is because the log undoes the e, or it inverts the e, and the e inverts or undoes the log.
cues.zh: 得到直線，是因為 log 會抵銷或反轉 e 的作用，而 e 會反轉或抵銷 log。

cues.en: So in fact, this is really just saying, you know, the log of e to the x is just x, and e to the log of x is just x.
cues.zh: 所以其實就是，e 的 x 次方取對數得到 x，而 e 的 log(x) 次方也得到 x。

cues.en: So in fact, what we're doing here is just a bizarrely complicated way of saying, plot x by x, which of course is just a straight line.
cues.zh: 因此，這裡只是用奇怪又複雜的方式，說要畫 x 對 x，當然就是直線。

cues.en: So, in this video, I introduced you to the intuition of natural exponent and natural logarithm, and I show that these are inverses of each other.
cues.zh: 這部影片介紹自然指數與自然對數的直覺，並說明兩者互為反函數。

cues.en: Again, logarithm is something you see very often in statistics and machine learning, in particular, for optimization of numbers, probability values that are very small.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，對數在統計與機器學習中很常見，尤其用於最佳化非常小的數字與機率值。
